app.title: Waikato World Model
app.description: Unofficial student-made 3D map of the University of Waikato's Hamilton campus, drawn from OpenStreetMap. Not affiliated with the University of Waikato.
app.ogDescription: See the University of Waikato's Hamilton campus on a 3D model of the place, drawn from OpenStreetMap. Unofficial; not affiliated with the University of Waikato.
app.noscript: Waikato World Model is an unofficial 3D map of the University of Waikato's Hamilton campus. It needs JavaScript and WebGL to run. It is not affiliated with the University of Waikato.
app.loadError: The map data could not be loaded. Check your connection and reload the page.
app.noWebgl: This browser could not start WebGL, so the 3D map is not shown. Search for buildings still works.
app.sceneLabel: 3D map of Waikato's Hamilton campus. Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag or two fingers to move.

about.unofficial: Waikato World Model is made by a student for students. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or maintained by The University of Waikato, and it uses no Waikato logo. Its colours are the project's own, the same for every school, and none is taken from Waikato. It shows the University's Hamilton campus from OpenStreetMap, and names a building as Waikato's only where OpenStreetMap says it is. For anything that matters, check Waikato's own campus maps and your own timetable.

limits.timetable: No class times. Waikato's online timetable is open to read, but its terms are on Waikato's main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, so they are unread and the site does not take the timetable. Nothing here is made up to fill the gap.
limits.timetableLoaded: Class times come from a snapshot of Waikato's timetable taken on {date}. Rooms and times change during the trimester; your own timetable is the authority.
limits.scheduled: A timetabled class is not the same as an occupied room. Classes are cancelled, moved and held online, and rooms are used for things that are not on the timetable.
limits.heights: Each of Waikato's buildings is one block on its OpenStreetMap outline, with no floors. Its height comes from OpenStreetMap: its height tag where it has one; else its number of levels, {height} m each; else 6.5 m, or 10 m for a building over 900 m², the defaults of the surrounding buildings. The building card says which. None of these heights is surveyed: OpenStreetMap gives the one building named here no height and no number of levels, so it stands at a default. The windows and the rim round each roof are drawn by rule and say nothing about the real walls and roofs. The ground's heights come from Land Information New Zealand's 8 m elevation model of 2012, which is drawn from contours: it is smooth bare ground, with sharp peaks a few metres low. A building stands on the ground under its middle; on a slope its uphill side goes into the hill and a footing fills the gap below the other side.
limits.rooms: No floors and no rooms. Waikato's campus maps are on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, so the site does not read them; its online timetable names rooms by code but gives no outline and no position. So each building is one block, and nothing inside it is drawn.
limits.campuses: The Hamilton campus is modelled. A building is drawn as Waikato's only where OpenStreetMap names the University of Waikato as its operator, or tags it as a university building, and gives it a name; any other stands among the surrounding buildings, with no name. On the Hamilton campus that is one building, the Gallagher Academy of Performing Arts. The campus's other buildings have names in OpenStreetMap but no tag that says whose they are, so they stand among the surroundings, unnamed, as does the medical school's building site, which OpenStreetMap names a construction site. Halls of residence and childcare centres stay unnamed among the surroundings. The Tauranga campus is not modelled: OpenStreetMap tags three buildings by Durham Street as a university's, but gives them no name and no operator, so no tag ties a building there to Waikato. Nor is Hangzhou in China, where Waikato teaches with a partner university.
limits.context: Surrounding buildings, streets and trees come from OpenStreetMap. Where it maps a building in parts or gives a roof a shape, those are drawn, the roof in a simplified form. Where a height is not mapped, a default is used. In the walker views every building, Waikato's and the rest, is drawn with storeys from its height, windows, and walls of plaster, brick, concrete, stone, glass or weatherboard chosen by rule from where it stands; none of it says what a real building looks like, and there are no doors, since none are mapped. The ground there is drawn by rule as well, on the streets, paths, railways, parks and ponds OpenStreetMap maps: asphalt with white lines, kerbs, paving slabs, steps, sleepers and rails, lawns and water, and grass and bare earth elsewhere. Its widths, lines and kerbs say nothing about the real ones, and there are no crossings, arrows or signs, since none are mapped. A tree standing alone is where OpenStreetMap maps it; its size and shape are drawn by rule, and in the walker views so are its leaves, its bark and the way it sways in a light breeze, the same every day; none of it says what kind of tree it is. Trees OpenStreetMap tags as deciduous turn in April and May, stand bare from June to August and come into leaf in September and October; the rest are drawn evergreen. Trees inside woodland areas are scattered for decoration.
limits.walker: The walker is a made-up figure, not a person: it stands for nobody, and nothing about where it goes leaves your browser. Its walks are planned round the buildings on the map and along OpenStreetMap's paths and streets, off motorways except over footbridges. Doors and entrances are not mapped, so a walk to a building ends beside its nearest wall, and it passes gates, fences and kerbs the map does not have. Its body is the "Animated Human" model by Quaternius, given to the public domain (CC0); its stance, trainers, hair, mouth, backpack and umbrella are drawn here by rule, in the project's own colours, none taken from Waikato. Where a building or a tree hides it, its shape shows through. An agent can steer it on your own computer through the scripts in the source code.
limits.subjects: No paper list. Waikato's paper pages and its Catalogue of Papers are on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, so the site does not take them.
limits.calendar: No trimester dates. Waikato's key dates are on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, so the site does not take them, and the time panel moves the sun and the light only.
limits.daylight: The sun stands where it does over Waikato's Hamilton campus at the date and time shown, from NOAA's published solar-position equations; below 10° above the horizon it is drawn at 10°, so that shadows stay on the map. Night falls as the sun goes from 6° above the horizon to 8° below. In Now mode the cloud, rain and fog follow Open-Meteo's current weather for Waikato's Hamilton campus, and the falling rain is drawn by rule; Preview shows a clear sky, because past and future weather are not known here.

about.privacy: The site has no accounts and sets no cookies. It holds no names of people. Only the copy at campusworldmodel.com is counted: there Cloudflare, which serves the site, counts page views and visits with its Web Analytics. It stores nothing in your browser and does not record which building you look at; a content blocker may stop it. If the weather line is shown, your browser asks Open-Meteo for the current weather at Waikato's Hamilton campus; nothing about you is sent beyond that request. A walk with the walker stays in your browser: where it goes, what it says and what it wears are not sent anywhere.

room.noTimetableWhy: Waikato's class times are not taken by this site, so it cannot say what is scheduled here. See About for details.

search.hint: Type a building's name, for example Gallagher Academy of Performing Arts. Rooms and papers are not shown: see About.
search.noResultsHint: Waikato's buildings are found by the names OpenStreetMap gives them, and only where OpenStreetMap says they are Waikato's. Building names work with or without macrons.

travel.go: Travel to {name}. This leaves Waikato World Model.
